title: Generation and ex vivo culture of murine and human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tissue slice explants
protocol: Chill a bottle of Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution and the Compresstome chilling block in a -20°C freezer for at least 30 minutes prior to tissue collection.
Weigh out 0.25 g low-melting agarose into a 50 mL flask.
Remove any residual glue residue from the Compresstome blade holder using acetone if necessary.
Cut a standard razor blade along the dotted lines marked horizontally to create a single-sided blade, then remove the top corners.
Adhere the prepared blade to the flat side of the Compresstome blade holder, flush against the lip of the blade holder, using a small amount of super glue.
Allow at least 20 minutes for drying and setting.
Soak the dried, cross-linked sponges in species-specific media to soften and absorb media components.
Trim base sponges into cubes approximately 1 cm thick using sterile forceps and scalpel.
Cut thin top sponges 2–3 mm thick using sterile forceps and scalpel.
Transfer trimmed base sponges into 24 well plates, each with 750 μL of species-specific explant media.
Soak sets of top sponges in approximately 2 mL of species-specific explant media per set.
Add any drugs or relevant treatment additives to the species-specific explant media before adding it to the sponges.
Pipette species-specific explant media on top of sponge rather than directly into well for better soaking from both sides.
Place plates in a 37°C incubator to allow full soaking within 30 minutes.
Humanely euthanize the animal as per your approved IACUC protocol.
Place the mouse on a dissection stage on its back and spray the torso with 70% ethanol to sterilize the skin and fur.
Cut through the skin and expose the abdominal wall (peritoneum) through blunt dissection with scissors.
Cut the peritoneum to open the abdominal cavity and locate the tumor.
Use sterile dissection scissors and/or scalpel to remove the tumor from the surrounding tissue.
Place the tumor in a sterile petri dish.
Remove any healthy pancreas tissue from the tumor if necessary.
Transfer the tumor to a 6-well plate with ice-cold Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution.
Store the tumor on ice.
Create a 2.5% w/v solution of sterile distilled water and low-melting agarose (10 mL H2O and 0.25 g agarose).
Microwave the solution until the agarose is fully dissolved.
Let the solution cool for approximately 1 minute until it is comfortable to touch.
Insert Compresstome white plastic plunger into metal casing, leaving an approximately 2–3 cm chamber.
Tape casing to plunger with lab tape and place the completed construct vertically in ice.
Use a transfer pipet to fill the specimen tube with agarose solution.
Using forceps, fully submerge the tumor tissue into the liquid agarose solution.
Insert the cold chilling block over the specimen tube and allow to incubate on ice for several minutes until the agarose solidifies.
Remove the sample from the cooling block before the agarose freezes, as indicated by crystals forming on the edges of the agarose.
Remove the specimen tube from chilling block and ice.
Insert tube into Compresstome tray through the hole in the side wall until flush with raised rim on tube.
Remove tape to release the plunger.
Connect the Compresstome tray to the base with the provided screw.
Add ice cold Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS) to tray to fully submerge the specimen tube.
Attach the blade holder to the vibration head with blade-side facing the control box and secure using the provided Allen wrench.
Press “Start” to begin sectioning.
Collect slices into cold HBSS in a 6-well plate on ice.
Remove remaining bulk tissue from the specimen holder with forceps.
Transfer remaining bulk tissue into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube with 1 mL 4% paraformaldehyde and incubate at 4°C for 2 h, then transfer to 70% ethanol at room temperature until paraffin embedding.
Fill sample mold halfway with Optimal Cutting Temperature Compound (OCT).
Transfer explant tissue into the OCT-filled mold and flatten as much as possible.
Fully cover flattened tissue with additional OCT.
Store OCT-covered tissue at -80°C.
Transfer thin, malleable tissue slices from buffer to culture sponge platform in a sterile environment.
Sterilize all instruments either autoclaved or washed with 70% ethanol and sterilized with flame.
Remove sponge plate from incubator to a sterile environment.
Use forceps to slide explant flat onto a spatula.
Transfer the explant slice to the sponge by touching the edge of the spatula to the sponge and using the forceps to slide the tissue onto the sponge.
Use forceps to place the thin top sponge over the tissue.
Place plate into 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Aspirate spent media from the well.
Replace aspirated media with 500 μL of fresh media directly into the well.
Mix any drugs or treatment additives in the fresh media before adding to the well.
Transfer explant into 2 mL microcentrifuge tube with 500 μL 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Incubate the sample at 4°C for 2 h.
Transfer the sample to 70% ethanol at room temperature until paraffin embedding.
Fill a sample mold halfway with Optimal Cutting Temperature Compound (OCT).
Transfer explant tissue and flatten as much as possible within the OCT.
Fully cover the tissue with additional OCT.
Store the OCT-embedded tissue at -80°C.
